system: You are an ambitious AI PhD student who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field of efficient computer vision architectures.
task_description: You are given the following file to work with, which implements and studies ConvNeur — a dual-branch vision architecture inspired by 'Efficiency Follows Global-Local Decoupling' (CVPR 2026). The architecture separates global context synthesis (via a lightweight neural memory branch) from local feature preservation (via a locality-preserving convolutional branch), combining outputs via a learned gate. The baseline is evaluated on image classification (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100) and measures accuracy, FLOPs, inference latency, and parameter count. The core research question is: how can the global-local decoupling principle be improved to achieve a better accuracy/efficiency trade-off? Particularly interesting ideas would: (1) challenge the assumption that two symmetric branches are optimal, (2) improve the learned gate mechanism, (3) reduce FLOPs while maintaining accuracy, or (4) demonstrate that the decoupling principle transfers to richer tasks. All changes should be measurable and reproducible within the provided training pipeline.
